meta.title: Who is in the global top 1%?
meta.units: international-$ per month (converted from daily at 365/12)
notes: Every country-bin inside the global top 1%, ranked by income. The marginal bin is clipped to the population still needed and flagged partial, so the listed populations sum to exactly 1% of the global total.
Population concept is basis-matched: adults for the per-adult series, total population otherwise, both from WID's demography.
Regions are PIP's own current scheme, with Western Europe split out of Europe and Central Asia using Western Europe (IHME GBD) — both from the ETL, so no hand-maintained mapping is involved.

regions.name: Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan and Pakistan

WID_posttax_rescaled.label: WID post-tax, rescaled to the ADJUSTED PIP country means (shape from WID, level from PIP_topadj — the far end of the PIP-side chain — so the bridge meets in the middle)

PIP_topadj.label: PIP on an income basis, top-adjusted (WID post-tax shape grafted above the splice bin, applied ON TOP of the consumption->income adjustment)

PIP_consinc.label: PIP adjusted to an income basis (consumption countries mapped via the dual-country regression)

PIP.label: PIP (disposable income or consumption, per capita)
